sections.title: What we're building
sections.text: Were designing a cozy isometric snowball fight game.  There are two teams, each team, has 4 players.  This is a single player game so I'm leaving it vague for you to decide.

sections.title: Decided (Foreman; host's calls outrank everything)
sections.text:
- 1 human + 3 AI allies (Pip, Scoop, Waffle) vs 4 AI. Match = first to 2 rounds of 120s (host): your hill, their hill, the park only at 1-1.
- Round: most crown-seconds with the toboggan. Sled starts beside the human in round 1, foot-centre in rounds 2–3. Every crown = same flat saddle. Tie → sudden death, capped 60s.
- Clock: afternoon → dusk (≥4 steps) → streetlights at 120s, plus a 20s countdown. Lighting resets each round.
- Camera: one fixed iso shot of the whole ~26m hill, kids ~48px at 720p. No pan.
- Controls (host): mouse only. Right-click walks to the cursor, left-click throws (hands off while carrying), middle-click builds.
- No elimination: a chilled kid warms up at the cocoa stand, ~8s, out of play. Target ≤2 chills per kid per round (bench + siege combined, <15%).
- Garage shop (host, rule 4): 4 credits per round played, +2 per round win, plus hits and crown time; one purchase per visit; ice 4, melter 4, rock 8, snowman 8, launcher 10. Gear and credits last the whole snow day (host), bots too; 'New snow day' wipes them, with a notice beside the button. A garage with nothing worth buying is one Continue click. Not yet built: bazooka, igloo, fort.
- Plain snowball = fast flat line, never clears a wall. Wall: one per kid, 1s plant at your feet, 8s cooldown (ghost footprint). Nothing built on the crown.
- Hits: first kid touched below head height in flight, or anyone in the ring at touchdown. One hit chills. No friendly fire.
- AI: Beanie, Pockets (blower), Brick (never throws), Copycat; fair-bot dodging.
- SIEGE: the crown holder faces one shared volley, ONE release frame per cadence, ≤4 live rings. Defenders 8m+ bracket the carrier's path; closer ones throw one direct shot. Cadence 2.0 / 1.5 / 1.45s per street; street 3 adds a second blower.
- FROSTY (host): bonus bout on 'Next street' / 'New snow day' (before the wipe). 60s, plain snowballs only, no building. 10 hits to melt him, you take 3. Specials at 15/30/45s (Burst, Burst, Double Blizzard) are instant loss outside a safe zone, with a 2.5s snowflake warning; the two mounds move at each wind-up. Prize: his pot hat on the porch screen.
- Session: up to 3 named streets (Maple Court, Ivy Terrace, The Summit Kids); gear carries across the day, nothing carries into a new snow day.

WAITING ON THE PLAYTEST: the two-slot loadout (rule 4) switches on only if street-3 chills per kid break ≤2 while street 1 clears it, or the launcher takes >60% of street-1 purchases (QA #32, #36).
NEXT: host playtests Frosty and persistent gear; Systems builds the siege and reruns the bot log.

sections.title: Hook: Snow Day (Creative v0)
sections.text:
Chestnut Street against three rival streets, three sledding hills each, and the streetlights are about to come on. Get the toboggan to the crown and hold it there longer than they do.
TONE: cozy = warm, silly, low stakes. Every upgrade is garage or kitchen junk: the launcher is a tennis-ball thrower, the rock is dirty plough ice, the bazooka is a cardboard-tube snow cannon. If it looks like a weapon ad, reskin it.
FIRST 30s: the whistle, sled 2–3m from your porch, everybody sprints. No tutorial; teach by racing.
LIGHT: the sky resets each round because it is the round clock, not the evening's.

sections.title: What a good throw feels like (Creative)
sections.text:
A snowball is a hard flat line (0.35s + 0.05s/m) arriving as the kid flinches; a free, watching kid at 6–10m is hit ≥60%. Reflex-dodging is NOT the skill.
1) The skill is the angle: a kid facing you sees it; one at your side, behind, or busy can't. A 30–45% match hit rate is healthy.
2) A plain ball NEVER clears a wall — walls are the reason to move. Only the blower (0.50s + 0.12s/m) arcs.
3) A miss looks like a near miss: it skids past the boots, ≥80% within 1.2m.

sections.title: Greybox verdict rules (QA) — decide before we look
sections.text:
Three first-timers, no coaching, one greybox match (first to 2 rounds of 120s, hill A, final camera, full dusk ending, porch screen). Temp audio: whistle, crunch, sled shout, release, impact, wall break, lights clunk; no sound for a landing ring. No audio = void session.

WATCH, nothing asked: 1) touches the sled within 20s; 2) hands off in minute 1 (QA #23); 3) builds unprompted in round 1, and whether a cooldown press stops them; 4) says who's winning at 35s and 105s; 5) porch button + hover time (QA #24); 6) what they look at while carrying (QA #25). Log the first unprompted complaint verbatim, with the minute.
STOPWATCH: seconds the human can't act (chilled, walking, at the stand; carrying counts as play). Target <15%; >25% = bench or walk too long.
CSV: human's crown-second share (QA #21); sudden-death rounds (>1 in 6 = scoring too flat); crown vs open-field chills.
AFTER: What told you time was running out (sky or countdown)? How did you know the sled changed hands? Lose sight of sled or kid? What changed the score? Best moment? What did you do when not carrying? Reopen the shop on purpose?

ONE FIX PER FAILURE:
- never touches the sled → cut a rule or move a spawn, never a prompt.
- never hands off → fix the ally wave, no text.
- never builds → cut the human's build; Brick keeps his walls.
- stops building after a cooldown press → bolder ghost footprint, no text.
- can't say who's winning → fix the score strip.
- loses the sled → camera or pennant failed; no new HUD.
- not in the score → move the round 2–3 sled toward Chestnut; never slow allies.
- 'Finish snow day' is NOT read from one match: with gear carrying over, the first Next also buys gear (QA #24). Read hover time across streets 1→2→3; only rising hover is a verdict. Then bucket possession changes by 30s: mostly in the first 60s = fix crown/geometry; late = the ending failed.

n=3 proves confusion, not fun. Fun verdict = the host playing a whole match.

objects.title: Core loop rules — Systems (numbers kept stable: 2 ruled out, 6b ruled out, 9 dropped with the cards)

entries.label: 1. Sled is carried, not camped
entries.text: Carrier: 60% speed, can't throw or build. No stealing: the sled changes hands only when a chilled carrier drops it in place (anyone may grab it) or by handoff (rule 6). A dropped sled doesn't score. Camping = slow, unarmed target, so teammates escort.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 2. Idle sled slides home
entries.text: Nobody touching the sled for 15s and it slides back to the bottom of the hill (kids shout). Score pauses. Kills the 0-0 turtle and forces someone to be the sucker.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 3. Sudden death
entries.text: Tie at the lights: first team to hold the crown 5 continuous s wins (a drop, chill or rival pickup resets it); after 60s, the first crown-second wins. The cap never pauses.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 4. Garage shop + economy
entries.text:
Between rounds only; every kid shops, bots too. Round 1 of street 1 = plain snowballs.
PERSISTENCE (host): upgrades and unspent credits last the whole snow day (all 3 streets), for every kid including the bots. 'New snow day' wipes everyone back to plain; the notice sits beside that button before the click: 'Fresh snow, fresh start — your gear and credits reset.'
CREDITS: 1 per hit, 1 per 6 crown-seconds, 4 per round played, +2 per round win.
PRICES: ice 4, melter 4, rock 8, snowman 8, launcher 10. Ice and rock share the ball slot.
GUARDS: one purchase per visit. Siege volleys always use the street's listed rings, never a bot's purchases (Fix 2). Spending never touches scoring.
GARAGE SCREEN (Art, default now): owned items read 'Owned — lasts this snow day', never priced again. If nothing is affordable or worth buying, it leads with 'Your gear is ready' and one Continue click to the next hill.
NAMED LEVER, OFF until the persistence gate (QA #32) trips: two-slot loadout. You keep everything you own but carry one throw (plain, ice, rock or launcher) and one build (wall or snowman); melter is passive, outside the slots. Never fix the launcher with its price (QA #36).
BOT WISHLISTS (first affordable): Beanie ice → launcher → rock; Pockets melter → snowman (keeps the blower); Brick melter only (he never throws); Copycat copies the human's last buy, else ice → launcher.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 5. Builds: snow wall by default
entries.text: Middle-click plants ONE low wall (1.5m) at your feet, facing your aim. 1s plant (busy); planting again moves it. 8s cooldown after any plant or break. Blocks flat throws; ice and rock break it. A bought snowman replaces it (rule 7). Igloo and fort: host-approved, not built yet.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 6b. Free-sled claim — allies never rob the human
entries.text:
Chestnut's three allies never claim a free sled while the HUMAN is the nearest Chestnut kid to it, for the first 4s the sled is free. They don't stop or wait: they run to support (crown, flank, wall) exactly as normal, and Pip still beats you to every loose sled you are not closest to. After 4s free, or the moment you are not nearest, ordinary Beanie logic applies and someone grabs it.

WHY: the round-1 sled sits 2–3m from the porch, so Beanie logic alone decides the first possession before a first-timer's hands are even on the keys — exactly the spectator case QA #21 measures. This is a possession-assignment clause, not bot hesitation: no animation, nothing on screen, fair-bot rule untouched, and rivals are exempt (Maple's Beanie will still sprint at YOUR free sled). Fails safe: if human carry share is still under 1/3, move the sled start, never make the allies slower.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 6. One order = handoff
entries.text: While carrying, left-click shoves the sled to the one outlined ally within 6m (carrier types only, never Brick). Otherwise it does nothing: no toss, cooldown or sound. Teacher: an eligible ally within 6m with no ring on them waves for the sled. No text.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 7. Throwing: aim a spot, hard line
entries.text:
Mouse aims a landing ring (r 0.8m); left-click throws. Ring visible to all from commitment; ball casts a shadow dot. Your ring hides while you carry; the handoff outline replaces it (QA #25).
- Plain: 0.35s + 0.05s/m, flat, 12m, NEVER clears a wall.
- Ice: 0.25s + 0.03s/m, flat, 12m, shatters the wall it hits.
- Rock: plain flight; smashes through walls and snowmen and keeps going; knocks a kid it chills 1.5m off the spot, away from the sled they dropped.
- Launcher: hold to spray: 0.3s + 0.04s/m, 9m, ring 0.45m, scatter ≤0.5m, 15-ball hopper, 2.5s reload. One pellet chills; balance by its own numbers, never its price (QA #36).
- Melter: walk into a rival wall/snowman to melt it. Touch a chilled teammate while they're frozen in place or still walking to the cocoa stand to thaw them on the spot (once per 6s). Once they reach the stand they're out of play and can't be thawed. Host's call; it restores 'heal a chilled ally'.
- Snowman: replaces your wall (3 hits, 12s cooldown); pelts rivals within 8m every 2.2s.
- Blower (Pockets): 0.50s + 0.12s/m, high lob, clears walls, 14m.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 8. Nothing gets built on the crown
entries.text: No walls inside the 4m crown circle or within 2m of the sled: no camping under cover.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 10. Session ladder — 3 streets; gear carries across the day
entries.text:
Snow day = up to 3 streets (~20 min); gear carries across them (rule 4). Plain rings: Beanie, Copycat; blower cappers: Pockets; Brick never throws.
Street 1 Maple Court: Beanie, Pockets, Brick, Copycat; siege 2.0s; 2 plain (lead + side) + 1 capper; reaction 0.60s.
Street 2 Ivy Terrace: same mix and rings; 1.5s; 0.50s.
Street 3 The Summit Kids: Beanie, 2 Pockets, Brick; 1.45s (floor); 1 plain lead + 2 cappers on both exits; 0.45s.
Max 4 live rings (QA #29).
After each match: equal 'Next street' / 'Finish snow day'; after street 3: 'New snow day' / 'Finish snow day'.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 11. Build numbers
entries.text:
Crown = same flat 4m radius on every hill; only approaches change. Greybox reaction 0.50s (log header).
SPEEDS: kid 4.5 m/s, carrier 2.7 m/s, no stamina or slope modifier. No dodge button: a dodge is walking out of a ring (right-click); a 0.8m step from standstill ≈ 0.25s.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 12. Camera: one fixed iso shot
entries.text: Whole ~26m hill in one 1280×720 frame (~49px/m, kids ~48px). No follow or pan; human, sled, crown, both porches and flanks always visible. Same footprint on all three hills. Each porch at the foot of its side; kids emerge in a 1.2m arc, human front-centre.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: 13. Busy vs free stance
entries.text: BUSY (planting) can't move. A CARRIER (2.7 m/s) clears 1.0m of ring in 0.37s, 2.0m in 0.74s, vs a free kid's 0.25s step (rule 11). That gap is why the siege bites and brackets come from range. The pose is the information.

entries.label: 15. Outcomes read as aftermath — ACCEPTED
entries.text: Spec in Art 'Feedback'. TEST: unlabelled 60s clip, ask 'how many throws missed?' None = misses aren't rendering; hit vs untouched unclear = chill state too subtle.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 17. Cocoa stand out of play — ACCEPTED
entries.text: TEST: log repeat-chills within 5s of returning; more than a couple = the stand is exposed, move it further off the hill.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 21. Is the human actually in the score?
entries.text: Pip and Scoop can win without the human. CSV: crown-seconds per carrier; share <1/3 is calibration. FAIL only if share <1/3 AND they credit only an ally's carry. FIX: move the round 2–3 sled 1.5m toward Chestnut; never slow allies.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 23. Handoff: count silent presses
entries.text: A failed handoff is silent. From the input log, count carrying throw-presses before the first success, per round: 1–2 = the wave taught it; 3+ = fix the wave (ally turns, arm higher), never a ring, number or tooltip; no handoff at all = 'never hands off'.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 24. 'Next street' is the verdict
entries.text:
Log button + hover seconds. Next fast = wants more; hovering ~10s then Finish = cost not worth paying; instant Finish = done. No prompting; Next never styled nicer than Finish.
PERSISTENCE CAVEAT (was #34): Next also buys gear for later hills, so the first Next is no verdict. Read hover time across streets 1→2→3: flat/falling = wants more hills; rising = pricing the button (and Frosty inherits the resentment).
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 25. Aim ring hidden while carrying — ACCEPTED
entries.text: TEST: ask what they watched while carrying and how they knew where rings would land. Watching their own cursor = the ring is stealing the siege read.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 26. Shop limits — ACCEPTED
entries.text: Limits in rule 4. TEST: does a first-timer reopen the shop unprompted? If not, it's a screen, not a system: cut prices, keep two items.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 28. Shop beginner fix — RULED
entries.text: Cheapest item = 4 = a no-hit, no-crown round (rule 4). Shop screen may use text (host). TEST: ask 'what could you afford?'; counting aloud twice = the screen isn't reading.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 29. Max live rings — RULED: cap 4
entries.text: A volley is held back if it would put >4 siege rings in flight on one carrier. CSV logs max live rings per carrier per round.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 31. Siege vs bench — RULED: one combined number
entries.text: A chill costs ~8s, so <15% allows two chills per round; a willing carrier's 2–3 holds can blow that while the crown works. Report human chills + bench seconds as one number. Bench >15% with holds at 8–20s: cut warm-up 8s → 5s first, move the stand second. Never shorten cadence for a bench number.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 32. Persistence gate (merged #32, #35, Systems)
entries.text: Read per street, the same player against their own street 1. TRIP: on street 3, chills per kid break the ≤2 rule (or bench >15%) while street 1 clears it. A win-rate jump is too weak to detect with n=3 (Systems), and 'zero swaps' can't fire while nothing needs swapping (QA #35). Split launcher chills from plain-ball chills in the CSV. ON TRIP: pull rule 4's two-slot loadout. Never retune the street tier or raise prices for this. Don't add shop items just to fill the shelf (Creative).
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 36. One item wins the day: launcher purchase share
entries.text: Persistence stretches the launcher over three streets for one payment, so 'save for the launcher, ignore the shelf' may be the only strategy. TEST: share of street-1 paid purchases by item. Launcher above ~60% = one item decides the day. RESPONSE: pull rule 4's two-slot loadout (the launcher becomes your one throw). Never raise its price; that only empties street 1 for first-timers.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 48px identity — one rig, four variants
entries.text: One rig, four head/coat silhouettes reused by both teams. Priority: head shape, team colour + scarf pattern, pose. Chestnut = burnt orange bands. Rivals by street: Maple Court = deep teal V; Ivy Terrace = plum dots; The Summit Kids = mustard zigzag (Foreman placeholders, Art may swap, but never a colour near orange). White overhead chevron = human only. Busy state from real carry/plant poses, no icon. Pennant on the sled, stays with a dropped sled. Charm goes in snowbanks and porch lights, not 48px detail.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: Throw readout
entries.text: Plain: short bright streak, dark underside, moving shadow; never a lob. Blower: raised ball, broken coral touchdown bracket. Preview stops at walls; footprint matches collision. No more warning layers before human testing.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: Score strip + ownership
entries.text: Pennant = carrier's team; dropped = white. Crown edge pulses each scoring second. Top strip: teams, crown-seconds, sled icon by the scorer, exact countdown in the last 20s; dusk and lamps reinforce it. Handoff preview outlines ONE eligible ally within 6m with a short sled arrow; never Brick.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: Greybox readability gate (human eyes, not telemetry)
entries.text:
Hill A, 1280×720, three unlabelled 1s clips (8-kid scrum / lob / wall interception) at sunset and dusk. A first-timer names human, carrier, leading team and incoming threat, then points to an escape; record errors and time.
FLANK: from each porch they point at the flank route within 1s, at dusk too.
MEASURE: kids ≥48px; landing footprint in projection; misses ≤1.2m for ≥80% (world-space CSV). The capture beats arithmetic.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: Feedback: aftermath + wall status
entries.text:
HIT: chilled, stopped kid + brief puff. MISS: ball resting at the end of its skid. WALL BLOCK: lasting dent, not a hole; only ice/rock break walls. Never hide chevron or pennant; no clouds or screen shake.
WALL STATUS: ghost footprint fills with the cooldown, full outline when ready, barred when illegal; never looks solid. The plant pose starts only on a legal plant.

entries.label: New-day reset notice — before commitment
entries.text: Beside 'New snow day', before the click, always visible: 'Fresh snow, fresh start — your gear and credits reset.' No confirm modal; Next street never shows reset copy. Avoid 'gear melted': garage junk doesn't melt.

entries.text: Pip (Beanie logic), Scoop (Pockets), Waffle (Brick). Same rig, orange bands, no new mechanics.

entries.label: Behaviour rules (Systems) — no state trees
entries.text:
Beanie: grabs a free sled, shortest legal path to the crown. Throws only when the sled has been off the crown 5s+. Never builds.
Pockets: blower only; holds 6–10m from the nearest enemy, faces their carrier, backs off inside 6m. Carries only as fallback.
Brick: never carries, receives or throws. Keeps his wall between his carrier and the nearest threat (outside the crown, ≥2m from the sled); wall down = walks 2m ahead as a shield.
Copycat: 2s after the human acts, repeats that action type; never initiates (copies the stand-in in bot runs).
SIEGE suspends Beanie's 5s rule and Copycat's never-initiate rule, for volley throws only (Host playtest 1).
FAIR-BOT: reacts only to committed rings in its ~120° front arc, after its reaction time, by walking 0.8m out (rule 11). Carriers and builders don't dodge.
Difficulty = street tier (rule 10); reaction 0.45–0.60s governs dodging only. Fallback carrier when Beanie is chilled 3s+: Pockets, then Copycat.
ALLIES: same logic. They never take a handoff the human didn't give, but a sled the human drops is free for anyone (6b stays ruled out).
SHOPPING: wishlists in rule 4.
STAND-IN (bot runs): Beanie logic, plain snowballs; in shop tests buys the item under test.

objects.title: Greybox bot round — logs and pass/fail (Systems)

entries.label: Record one CSV, one fixed seed
entries.text:
Every row tagged with snow day, street (1–3), match and round. Per second: sled state, both scores. Per throw: thrower, item, distance, ring position, flight time, outcome (hit / wall / empty / stepped out), target facing and busy. Per volley: shared release-frame ID. Per miss: closest approach. Per kid per round: chills, split by the item that caused them (launcher vs plain vs other), bench seconds, credits. Per garage visit: street, credits held, item bought or none, Continue clicks. Per round, 30s buckets: possession changes and handoffs.
Conditions: run whole snow days so kits carry over exactly as in play; stand-in in the human slot. The siege gate uses street 1 (0.60s); other checks use 0.50s.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Pass/fail — does the loop exist
entries.text: Sled on the crown 25–60% of the round; ≥6 possession changes per round; longest hold ≤25s, else camping: fix geometry or a rule, never HUD. Log siege volleys (count, rings, hits).
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Pass/fail — are the decisions real
entries.text:
Clear a ring = reaction + 0.25s step + 0.1s slop (0.95 / 0.85 / 0.80s by street).
Free, facing kid at 6–10m: hit ≥60% (<50% = flight time wrong). Busy or flanked: ~100%.
Match hit rate 30–45%: >60% = bots blind; <25% = no flank route, fix geometry.
Chills: 4–8 per team per round, ≤2 per kid (2 × 8s = 13% of 120s); a 3rd is a geometry/spawn report. Count crown-hold chills apart from open-field.
Misses: ≥80% within 1.2m; a ball through a body is a collision bug.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Shop phase: per-item win rate, one retune then delete
entries.text: Per item: 30+ matches (0.50s, hill A) with the stand-in forced to buy it, vs plain-snowball control on the same seeds. Outside 40–60% win rate: one retune of the item's own numbers (range, rate, cooldown), then cut. Never a price change for the launcher (QA #36); for other items price is the last resort.

entries.label: Wall-block share
entries.text: Share of plain throws that die on a wall. <25%: ship. 25–35%: watch, shorten the flank. >35%: walls are the game; fix geometry (wider flank) or a slower rebuild, not a new item.

objects.title: Siege (Host playtest 1: the crown was too safe)

entries.label: Diagnosis (from greybox/src/sim/ai.ts)
entries.text: Vs a human on the crown only Pockets attacked (one blower per 8s). Beanie waits for a drop, Copycat mirrors throws a carrier can't make, Brick never throws: 3 of 4 rivals passive while the human scores.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Fix 1: Siege — one shared volley, not per-bot cadences
entries.text:
TRIGGER: an enemy carries the sled within 2m of the crown edge; ends when it's dropped, carried 2m+ away, or retaken.
Every free defender (not chilled, carrying or planting) joins ONE shared volley timer, so each volley is one visible event. AI exceptions in the behaviour rules; Brick never throws.
SYMMETRIC: Pip/Scoop/Waffle siege a rival carrier the same way.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Fix 2: Bracket — lead from range, direct shot up close
entries.text:
One volley = every free thrower's ring on the SAME frame. Rings come from the street tier (rule 10), never a bot's bought item, so the 4-ring cap holds.
FAR (8m+) plain: lead = carrier position + velocity × flight time, plus a ring 1.2m to one side.
NEAR (<8m): one direct shot, no lead.
CAPPERS (blowers) land ~1s late on the obvious exit; street 3's two cover both.
Bracket punishes running straight, near shot standing still, capper the obvious exit: irregular walking is the skill. Stepping out of a ring inside the crown keeps you scoring. Handoff is the free escape. All rings visible from release, no homing.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Gate (don't overcorrect)
entries.text:
Loop gates still hold. NEW: a willing carrier's median street-1 crown hold is 8–20s (≥12 holds over 6 rounds); no carrier chilled by two volleys in a row more than twice per round. Log thrower distance per siege ring: most crown chills from <8m = near rule missing.
Never survives 8s → lengthen the volley period. Crown never held → fix geometry (cover outside the crown or a 2m no-throw band). Holds past 20s → add a capper before shortening cadence.
RETUNE one lever at a time: capper count → cadence (1.45–2.0s) → lateral spacing (1.2m). Never shrink the 0.8m ring.

entries.label: Frosty: 60s, 10 hits to melt, you can take 3 (host)
entries.text: Your kid alone vs Frosty on the crown, 60s, streetlights on. He never moves or dodges and is big and easy to hit; 10 hits melt him, his 3rd hit on you (or the clock) ends it. A hit on you = knockback + cancelled throw, never the cocoa stand. PLAIN SNOWBALLS ONLY, NO BUILDING: the launcher would erase his 10 hits and your wall would bypass the moving mounds.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Specials: Blizzard Burst, then Double Blizzard (RULED)
entries.text:
NORMAL: aimed volleys at you (lead ring + direct ring + lob); a hit = one of your 3. They pause for the whole special.
SCHEDULE (fixed by the clock, not by hits): 15s Blizzard Burst, 30s Blizzard Burst, 45s Double Blizzard. 2s dizzy after each (free throws).
BLIZZARD BURST: gapless ring of flat snowballs in every direction; instant loss unless you're in a drawn safe zone (host).
DOUBLE BLIZZARD: one relocation, one warning, then two bursts ~1.5s apart from the same cover. First 'run now', then 'stay put'; stepping out between them to steal a throw is the greed trap.
WARNING: 2.5s snowflake swirl tight around Frosty, bigger and louder each half-second, a different pose per special. Nothing fires without the full swirl.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Shelter moves when he winds up (host) — RULED timing
entries.text:
Two snow mounds. Each special starts with a 0.5s mitten sweep: old mounds sink, snow puffs mark where the new ones rise (show the destination first). New mounds are fully formed BEFORE the 2.5s swirl, then locked; nothing moves mid-warning or mid-impact.
Random placement, but one mound is always 5–7m from your kid, so the run always fits.
Safe zone drawn in the snow. Mounds stay put between specials. His lob clears them, your plain ball can't: cover and firing position are opposite sides of the same mound.

entries.label: Prize: Frosty's pot hat on the porch screen (RULED)
entries.text: Win: Frosty's pot hat + 'You melted Frosty' beside your street on the porch screen for the rest of the snow day (up to 3). A hat won after street 3 shows on that day's final porch card, then the new day starts clean. Nothing on the field (it would read as the bought snowman). No power or credits: a bonus never touches balance.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Losing costs nothing
entries.text: Caught by a special or his 3rd hit: a kid-shaped snowdrift pops out your hat, then a mitten. Win: Frosty slumps into a heap, pot on top. Nothing lost; a bonus, never a tax.

entries.label: Placement: 'Next street' plays it, 'Finish' skips it
entries.text: After the porch screen, so it never muddies the Next/Finish read (#24). 'Next street' / 'New snow day' plays it, then the whistle; 'Finish snow day' skips it. No third button. On 'New snow day' the bout plays BEFORE the wipe, so the old day's porch card still gets its result. If Next-choosers quit mid-bout, drop to 2 specials first (Tuning); the 60s clock stays.

entries.label: Tuning + what to log (RULED)
entries.text:
BUDGET: Blizzard Burst ~5.5s without normal throwing (0.5 sweep + 2.5 warning + release + 2 dizzy), Double ~7s: ~18s total, leaving ~42s of throwing plus ~6s dizzy windows. At ~1 hit per 2.5s under fire, 10 hits fits a player who throws in the open and spends 1–2 of 3 hit points. Skilled fit, not a sure win.
RED LINES: median 1–2 hit points spent. 0 in most bouts = strengthen the normal volley. Most end at 3 hits taken = lengthen the gap between specials. First-timer median <8 hits at the buzzer = drop to 2 specials (20s, 40s). The 10 is the host's call; never change the 2.5s warning or the 60s clock.
LOG: hits landed by second; hits taken normal/special; swirl-start-to-safe seconds; throw gap across each special.

entry.label: 6b. Free-sled claim — allies never rob the human
entry.text:
Chestnut's three allies never claim a free sled while the HUMAN is the nearest Chestnut kid to it, for the first 4s the sled is free. They don't stop or wait: they run to support (crown, flank, wall) exactly as normal, and Pip still beats you to every loose sled you are not closest to. After 4s free, or the moment you are not nearest, ordinary Beanie logic applies and someone grabs it.

WHY: the round-1 sled sits 2–3m from the porch, so Beanie logic alone decides the first possession before a first-timer's hands are even on the keys — exactly the spectator case QA #21 measures. This is a possession-assignment clause, not bot hesitation: no animation, nothing on screen, fair-bot rule untouched, and rivals are exempt (Maple's Beanie will still sprint at YOUR free sled). Fails safe: if human carry share is still under 1/3, move the sled start, never make the allies slower.

chat.text: ok guys, another day..  I am testing seeding, I seeded the board with the general direction for the game.  Remember fun first, don't over complicate things.  Consider the user experience the most important thing.  Have fun!

I've set up the board for the team:

- **Brief:** added a "Working assumptions" box as a starting point to argue with: 1 human and 3 AI teammates against 4 AI rivals, best of 3 short rounds, credits spent in a shop between rounds but not used as the final score, and controls kept to move, aim/throw and one build key.
- **Open problems:** new amber group with an owner on each item:
  - Systems: pick one win condition.
  - Creative: rock snowballs and bazookas clash with "cozy".
  - Systems: cut 5 weapons + 3 structures down to about 3 real choices.
  - QA/UX: how the player directs AI teammates.
  - Art: make throw arcs readable from the isometric angle.
- **One fix:** "End Game" said "open question" but was ticked as agreed, so I unticked it.

**Note to the team:** please argue against my assumptions rather than add to them. A new feature only goes in if it replaces a weaker one. The seed has one hidden trap: if credits are both the score and the money you spend, buying anything lowers your score. Systems, fix that first.

**Scores:** coherence 4, novelty 4, feasibility 7, fun 5. These are low because we have no core loop yet.

**Next round's focus:** pick one win condition and a core 3-minute round loop that's fun with plain snowballs before any upgrades are added.

The hook I'm planting: **Snow Day** — two streets, one sledding hill, and the streetlights are about to come on. You win by holding the toboggan at the top for the most time before dusk, so nobody's eliminated (chilled kids just warm up at the cocoa stand and jog back) and the timer is something you can *see* in the sky rather than a HUD bar. I also solved the tone clash by reskinning instead of cutting: the rock is a chunk of dirty ice the plow left, the bazooka is a leaf blower, and the melter is a thermos of cocoa — cozy and silly, nothing reads as a gun. I put the shell of the 3-minute round on the flowchart and trimmed the weapon list to three.

Systems: take the win condition apart. Hill-time with a soft timer — does holding the toboggan actually create a good decision every 10 seconds, or does it collapse into both teams camping the top? If it needs a rule to stop a stalemate, tell me now and I'll find a cozier answer than a "contested" timer.

Confirmed the sled — with one change: it's **carried, not camped**. The carrier is slow and can't throw, so holding the crown costs you your defense and forces the team to escort. That makes every 10 seconds a decision: who's the sucker, and who covers them? Also added: idle sled slides home after 15s (kills the 0-0 turtle), independent round scoring (5 continuous seconds wins a tie), credits as shop money only, and structures cut to one snowball wall — igloo and snowman added rules, not choices.

Open problems on the win condition are ticked. Remaining: player commands (QA) and iso arc readability (Art).

Challenge for QA: keep commands to **one context order** — my AI already reacts to who carries the sled, so I'd argue the human needs a "you! take it" ping and nothing else. If we need a radial menu, we got the design wrong.

(my turn failed: 0 endpoints out of 1 requested are available matching your guardrail restrictions and data policy. We removed them for the following reasons (an endpoint may have matched multiple reasons):
Paid model training violation (account settings): 1 endpoint excluded; configurable at https://openrouter.ai/settings/privacy)

Four risks posted to the board, plus the ally-command question closed: the answer is the **handoff** — while carrying, the throw key shoves the sled to the kid you're aiming at, which is both the only order and the carrier's only button. Systems, that's your "you! take it" ping without a menu (radial menus now ruled out).

My independent challenges: "carried, not camped" may still be camping, since standing still on the crown pays 1/sec — your counter that a slow unarmed target dies fast is a hypothesis, so log how long the holder stands still in a bot round. Eight similar kids in iso also means players can't see who's ahead or who's holding, so the sled needs a filling flag and a scarf outline, not a HUD bar. And crown-time credits currently pay the team that's already winning — I'd make intermission credits flat 3 + 1 per hit.

Muse, when your endpoint works: the flag-fills-with-seconds and sky-dims-in-visible-steps question is yours, and it decides whether the last 20 seconds actually feel like panic.

I turned the decisions into a short "Decided" list in the Brief and cleaned up behind it. QA's flat-credit fix is now in Systems rule 4 and the sled handoff is in rule 6. I deleted the QA notes and resolved problems that are now covered, and accepted QA's readability fix with Art as owner. The board flagged the handoff as close to the ruled-out order menu, but that ruling allowed one context action and the handoff is exactly that, so it stays.

That leaves three open problems:
- **Systems + Art:** one throw key has to pick between a flat throw and a lob. If lobs are free, walls are useless.
- **Systems:** the shop is the weakest mechanic. It's seen only once or twice a match, and we haven't said who buys, whether the AI buys, or whether upgrades last. Define it in one line or I cut it.
- **Creative:** we need a cheap source of variety between matches.

**Scores:** coherence 7, novelty 5, feasibility 7, fun 6. Fun is a guess until someone plays a bot round.

**Next round's focus:** settle how throwing works (tap vs hold, and how lobs read from the isometric angle). It's the main thing the player does and it's still undefined.

Replay variety, answered with zero new mechanics: **best of 3 is the variety** — round one on your hill (short, easy to defend), round two on theirs (steeper, ugly angles), round three in the park (open, no cover). Geometry changes, rules never do, so the rounds stop feeling like reruns and start feeling like a story: defend home, invade, settle it. I gave the streets names — Chestnut vs Maple Court — because names are free identity and the hook reads better with them.

On the throw question I'm pushing back on tap-vs-hold: a wind-up key makes kids throwing balls feel like a charged rifle. Make the arc a property of the ball instead — snowballs are flat up close and auto-lob only at long range (so slow you can walk out from under), ice chunks are always flat and break walls, and the leaf blower always lobs. One key, no mode, and walls still matter.

Art: if the long lob is automatic and slow, can a player actually see it coming and step aside in the iso view? If not, the lob is unfair and my answer breaks — tell me and I'll fix it from the fantasy side rather than stacking a HUD indicator on top.

Both open problems are closed.

**Throw (rule 7):** Creative's answer wins — no tap/hold. You aim a landing ring and release; flight time is 0.3s + 0.12s per metre, so the arc grows with distance by itself. A 1.5m wall is only cleared by balls that are already high as they pass it, i.e. rings ~5m past it. Walls stop the close game and nothing else, and the ice chunk sweeps through them. **Art's question, answered from systems:** the readout is the ground, not the ball — everyone sees the landing ring the moment a throw commits, so a 1.3s lob is dodgeable on sight. No HUD indicator needed.

**Shop: I cut it.** Credits bought us one decision per intermission at the cost of a currency, a screen and AI buying logic. Replaced with a garage draft: 2 junk cards, pick 1, lasts the match. Foreman, that kills the "credits = shop money only" line in your Decided box — please strike it.

**Also ruled:** you can't build a wall inside the crown circle (QA risk #2 fixed by geometry instead of tuning). Question for Creative: with no currency and only two drafts, are three junk items enough, or does round 1 feel identical to round 2?

Added a storybook gameplay concept: orange stripes versus teal chevrons, oversized mittens, warm windows, and readable silhouettes. Its caption flags generation mistakes—especially the crown appearing as a pit; builders should use flat snow.

I challenge the flag-only scoreboard: it shows ownership, not both accumulated scores, so I proposed a compact score strip and exact final-20-second countdown. Aim previews should also stop at blocking walls rather than promise impossible landings.

QA/Systems: can snowballs hit kids mid-flight? If yes, a landing ring alone cannot reliably warn the player.

Art's question has a cheap ruling I'd defend: a ball hits the first kid it touches in flight *or* anyone inside the ring at touchdown, no friendly fire — that's affordable because close flat throws are over in ~0.4s (reflex, and the ball is right there) while every long throw is a slow lob that stays above head height until its own ring, so the ground ring really is the honest warning for anything you could react to. Landing-only hits would have players watch balls pass through their kid and call it broken.

I conceded the scoreboard to Art's pennant-plus-strip (my worry was legibility of a moving score, not layout) and posted three new risks: what my three buttons do after a draft (the cocoa thermos currently has no rule at all, and nobody's said whether a drafted card replaces the wall key), and how long a chilled beginner is actually benched — mid-hill cocoa stand, ~8s total, or round 1 is a walk in the cold.

Foreman: the Decided box still says "Credits = shop money only" and Systems' draft killed credits — strike it, and if Creative can't one-line the thermos by next round, cut it so the draft isn't picking from one real card.

I took the credits line out of the Decided box and rewrote it as one list of the current rules: the garage draft, the three hills, about 8 seconds out of play when chilled, and QA's ruling on what counts as a hit. I adopted QA's fixes for the buttons and for time on the bench. I also gave the cocoa thermos a one-line rule: it's passive, and it absorbs your first hit each life. I didn't make it a melt zone, because that would let a team turn the crown into a bunker and undo Systems rule 8. I deleted the problems that are now solved and the duplicate scoreboard entry.

There are two new open problems, and they're the real risk now:
- **The AI is the game:** 7 of the 8 kids are bots, and we haven't specified how the enemy AI behaves at all.
- **Crown scrum:** players come back fast and there's one hilltop, so all 8 kids may pile into a 4m circle where nobody can read anything.

**Scores:** coherence 8, novelty 5, feasibility 6, fun 6.

**Next round's focus (Systems, QA checks it):** a one-line role spec for each of the 4 enemy kids: who rushes the crown, who builds walls, who goes after the carrier, and how they dodge incoming rings.

Answered Systems' draft worry with zero new cards: **each hill deals its own pair** — your garage gives ice chunk + leaf blower, their yard gives blower + thermos, the park gives chunk + thermos. Same three cards, three different picks, and round two feels *foreign* because your favourite card isn't on the table.

I also fought the thermos out of its passive corner. "Absorb the first hit" is invisible and will always lose the draft, so make the flask your ball: aim at a chilled teammate, throw, and they're back on their feet warm instead of walking to the cocoa stand. It reuses the handoff rule exactly, it can't make the crown a bunker because it targets a kid rather than a zone, and it's the coziest move in the game — you bean your friend with cocoa to get them back in the fight.

For the AI I wrote the spec as people: **Beanie** always wants the sled, **Pockets** never comes within 6m, **Brick** only builds, **Copycat** does whatever you just did. Systems can turn each obsession into one behaviour rule, and the player learns all four by watching, not reading.

On the scrum, fix it with ground rather than UI: make the crown a ridge with two narrow approaches so eight kids funnel instead of pile. Systems and QA — once the flask is an option, does the human still have a reason to throw at kids, or does he just become the team medic?

AI is ruled: each Maple kid's obsession became one line, no state trees, and all of them share exactly two numbers — reaction time to a landing ring (0.25–0.6s) and dodge chance (30–80%). That's the whole difficulty slider, and Brick plus Pockets are what finally make escorting the carrier a real fight rather than a formality. Fallback carrier order (Pockets → Copycat → Brick) means the objective is never idle when Beanie is chilled.

**On the thermos, my answer to Creative:** be the medic, but it costs your offence — the flask *is* your ball. You can't shoot the incoming Beanie and heal your escort in the same life, so the medic is a role, not a free aura. Rule 9 on the board.

**Challenge for Art:** the crown scrum may be a scope answer, not a UI answer — if the hilltop needs a ridge with two narrow approaches to stay readable, that's level geometry we should prove in the same 720p gate, before anyone builds a warning system to fix a scrum we designed.

Narrow approaches may concentrate the scrum rather than solve it, so I specified a broad-saddle versus pinched-ridge greybox test and added a comparison image; its caption flags generation errors, not instructions to copy.

Copycat now mimics your pose, not your team colours—deliberately misreading allegiance would sabotage our readability goal. I also corrected my earlier feedback spec: touchdown has an area hit, so its bracket must show that actual footprint.

QA: can the broad saddle pass the one-second human/carrier/escape-route check without extra UI, while avoiding longer stationary-carrier stretches?

Art, answered on his own entry: the one-second gate is about silhouettes and eyelines, not approach count — broad saddle A can pass with zero extra UI if the crown shoulders stay below kid height and no two bodies overlap the rim, and the stationary-carrier log is driven by Pockets' lobs and bot reaction times, not hill shape, so don't buy geometry to fix an AI number.

New on my shelf: **cut the 30–80% dodge chance** and keep reaction time alone — a bot steps out only if it can physically reach the ring's edge in the time left, so dodges are visible movement and hits are earned. Also, round 1 should place the sled 2–3m from the human's porch in their lane, or "teach by racing" means the beginner watches seven bots learn the game without them. And I'd watch the draft for a single right answer: if the ice chunk is just the best ball, repair it by making walls cheaper for everyone instead of buffing lob damage.

Systems: if you accept reaction-time-only dodging, your difficulty slider shrinks to one number and Beanie becomes genuinely scary instead of lucky. Foreman: what's the first thing you'd actually build — one hill of greybox with eight bots, or the readability pass?

I approved the thermos as Creative and Systems pitched it (rule 9): the flask is your ball and it heals a chilled ally. My passive version would have lost every draft. I also accepted QA's ideas to cut dodge chance (reaction time is now the only difficulty number) and to start the round 1 sled next to the human.

I fixed a few contradictions:
- **Draft:** the "your garage" pair could never be dealt, because there's no draft before round 1. The two draft picks would also have given you two balls, so now you hold one card and only the human drafts.
- **Brick's walls:** his 3 walls broke the one-wall rule that applies to everyone, so he now gets one like the player.
- **Ally AI:** our 3 allies now reuse Beanie/Pockets/Brick (one AI codebase), replacing the old escort logic.

QA, what we build first: greybox hill A with 8 bots and plain snowballs, and run every log and the 720p readability check on that same build. Cards come second and art third; that order is now in the Brief.

Remaining open problem for Systems: what the flask can actually target when chilled kids leave for the cocoa stand within ~8s. The new entry has a proposal.

**Scores:** coherence 8, novelty 6, feasibility 7, fun 6. I'm not raising fun until a bot round is logged.

**Next round's focus:** Systems, settle the flask's target window and the bot-round script (the logs to capture and pass/fail numbers for each) so the greybox can be built against it.

I'm killing my own flask. If a card needs a "target window" spec to work, it isn't a fun verb — it's paperwork — so swap it for **the snow shovel**: your wall goes up instantly and free instead of an 8s rebuild. Nothing new to learn, useful every fight, and it finishes the triangle: ice chunk breaks walls, leaf blower floats over them, shovel gives you more of them. Cocoa already carries that coziness at the chilled kid's stand; the flask was the same warmth twice.

On the crown: greybox **A (broad saddle)** wins on fantasy, not just readability — that's what the top of a sledding hill looks like and it's where a toboggan stops; a pinched ridge reads as a mountain, and kids don't climb mountains.

Systems: rule the shovel in or rebut it in one line, because rule 9 is still standing for a card I've withdrawn. And on the draft, I'd keep only this from my deleted idea — the two cards on offer at intermission 2 belong to the hill you're about to play, so your favourite isn't always on the table.

**Shovel ruled in.** It adds no mechanic, it changes one number — instant, free, re-plantable wall, still one wall and still nothing on the crown. That's the only card we can implement before the greybox and still show a real choice.

**Bot-round script is on the board** (three entries): one CSV with a fixed seed and mid difficulty, and the numbers that decide go/no-go — crown occupied 25–60% of the 180s, at least 6 hand-offs, no single hold over 25s, 6–12 kids chilled per team, 35–60% hit rate at 6–10m, and at least half of all misses coming from someone physically stepping out of the ring. If bots dodge by moving, we've proven the landing ring is the game's verb; if they dodge invisibly, we haven't.

**QA's dodge cut is accepted** — reaction time alone, and a bot only steps out if it can reach the ring's edge in the time left.

One stale line for Foreman: the Decided box and the card list still name the cocoa thermos. I've rewritten the card entry to the shovel, but the Brief is yours.

Added a placeholder silhouette sheet for the greybox—not a final-art detour—and made the readability gate an actual first-time-viewer test. Bot telemetry can measure pacing, but cannot establish human readability or human downtime.

The shovel has a concrete risk: instant, free rebuilding could negate every ice-chunk hit through wall-button spam. Systems, can it instantly relocate an intact wall while retaining the shared 8s recovery after destruction? That preserves mobile cover without turning it into a flickering shield.

Art's flicker question has a one-line fix: make shovel walls plant **at your feet**, instantly and free, one at a time with a ~3s cooldown, and keep the shared 8s after a break — the flicker only exists because placement is remote, and planting where you stand is both cheaper and cozier (you physically carry your cover up the hill, and rule 8 still keeps it off the crown). But that flips my draft worry rather than settling it: the shovel is now the only card that gives mobile cover while flat throws are most of the game, so I'd log per-card win rates in cards phase and delete anything outside 40–60% instead of nerfing it into a second ice chunk.

Bigger catch on the build: Systems' own pass criterion — "at least half of misses are the target stepping out of the ring" — is unmeasurable unless the landing ring and first-contact hits ship in the greybox, so cards can wait but the ring and wall can't. I also struck the "<15% human unable to act" line from the bot CSV (there's no human in it) and moved it into a real session: three first-timers, no coaching, answering do they find the carrier in 1s, touch the sled in 20s, press the wall key unprompted, and know who's winning at 60s.

Foreman: the Decided box still lists the cocoa thermos and "throw doubles as flask" — worth one cleanup line before Systems builds against it.

I approved the snow shovel using QA's version: you plant the wall at your feet, instantly and free, with about a 3s cooldown, and a broken wall still waits 8s. That closes Art's worry about walls flickering in and out. The thermos is now on the ruled-out list, and the Brief and rule 4 no longer mention it. Phase 1 now also includes the landing ring, first-contact hits and the wall, because QA spotted that the bot log can't measure dodging without them. I struck the human-downtime line from the bot log, since that round has no human in it, and deleted the six entries that had been merged or settled.

**Biggest gap left:** nothing makes anyone play a second match. I opened a problem for Creative and Systems with the smallest fix I could think of: a street ladder, where each street you beat leads to a faster, differently mixed team, with no unlocks.

**Scores:** coherence 8, novelty 6, feasibility 8, fun 6.

**Next round's focus:** settle what carries over between matches in one line, or argue convincingly that the game doesn't need it.

Progression, in one line: **nothing carries over.** No unlocks, no currency, no stats — a match is three rounds on three hills, about ten minutes, and that's already a session. What carries is the story: the hill keeps the winner's pennant for the rest of the session, so match 2 opens with someone else's colours on your crown, and the ladder doesn't grow you — it grows the rivals, same four obsessions in the next street's colours with faster reaction times. You don't get stronger; you meet worse kids, and the whole cost is a scarf palette.

That's also the smallest honest answer to "why play again" — one texture and a grudge, rather than a second currency to design, balance and localise.

Art: the flag is now the memory of the whole session, so it has to survive your one-second gate — standing on the crown, can a first-timer say whose colours are on the pole without a caption? If it can't, the pennant needs a silhouette shape per street, not just a colour swap, and I'd rather know that now than after the greybox.

**Progression ruled (rule 10):** nothing carries over, and the ladder reuses the dial we already have — reaction time 0.60s for street 1 down to 0.35s for street 5, same four obsessions, same three hills, same cards. Only the scarf and one number change, and a cleared street leaves its pennant on the pole so match 2 opens with enemy colours on your crown.

**Art's flicker worry is closed** by QA's version, which Foreman already approved: a shovel wall plants at your feet, instant and free, 3s cooldown, and after a break the shared 8s still applies. Mobile cover you physically carry, not a remote shield.

I also logged the card phase: 30+ matches per card, anything outside a 40–60% win rate gets deleted rather than nerfed — the shovel is the first suspect.

Foreman, one number to decide: five streets at ~10 minutes is a 50-minute session with no save. Do we want the ladder capped at three streets, or is a long session the point?

The history flag creates a new ambiguity: a previous winner’s colours on the crown could look like current possession. I proposed keeping history on the porch/results screen and reserving the moving sled pennant for live ownership, with square/stripe versus notched/V identities; the new image explores that distinction.

For session length, each match should end satisfyingly with equally clear “Next street” and “Finish snow day” choices—not require a 50-minute ladder.

QA: can first-timers distinguish “who won last match?” from “who holds the sled now?” without coaching? Live-possession mistakes should block release; forgotten history should not.

Art, my answer is no — don't test it, delete it: with eight kids in matching coats on one hilltop, a first-timer asked two questions about the same pole answers one and guesses the other, and the wrong guess is "the enemy holds the sled," which is the most expensive misread we can ship. Keep history on the results screen and the porch sign, keep the pole as live ownership only, and put the grudge in the intermission card where nothing is moving.

On the ladder I think there's a real math problem: street 5 reacts in 0.35s and needs about 0.6s total to clear a ring, but a 6m throw flies 1.02s — so Pockets dodges everything from range, high streets collapse into a scrum, and the leaf blower goes dead exactly when the player is best with it. Cap the reaction dial at 0.45s and spend the rest of the difficulty on team **mix**, which is code we already have and is visible on screen, so the player can say why a street is harder; and make 3 streets / ~30 min the default session with "next street" and "finish snow day" as equal buttons.

Foreman: I'd like one rule about what a bot is allowed to dodge — if a bot can leave the ring after the ball's flight is committed, the ring stops being a promise, and that's the thing we've built the whole game on.

I've settled progression and the bot rules, and the Brief now matches:

- **Session ladder:** a snow day is 3 streets, about 30 minutes. Bot reaction time goes 0.60s, then 0.50s, then 0.45s as the floor. Street 3 is also harder through its team mix (2 Pockets, no Copycat). After each match, "Next street" and "Finish snow day" are equal buttons.
- **History flag:** the previous winner's pennant on the crown pole is now ruled out. QA and Art are right that players would read it as "the enemy holds the sled". The grudge goes on the intermission card and the porch sign instead.
- **Fair-bot rule (answers QA's question):** bots see only what the player sees. They react only to rings already thrown, only inside a roughly 120° arc in front of them, and they move at human speed. Kids who are carrying the sled or building a wall don't dodge.

I also deleted the six entries these rulings replaced.

QA's math reaches further than the ladder. Even a street 1 bot that's facing you and not busy can step out of any 6m throw. So with plain snowballs, hits at range only land from the side or behind, or on a busy kid. That might be a great skill, or it might make throwing feel futile.

**Scores:** coherence 8, novelty 6, feasibility 8, fun 6. Fun is still unproven.

**Next round's focus (Systems):** rerun the hit-rate math under the fair-bot rule. Then either confirm the 35–60% ranged hit-rate target or replace it with one that says what a good throw should feel like.

Throwing shouldn't be fixed with a bigger landing ring — it should be fixed with flight time. A snowball should be a **hard flat line that arrives just as the kid flinches**, so dodging is something a bot does *before* the ball, never after. I've put a concrete feel-target on the Brief for Systems: plain ball ≈ 0.35s + 0.05s/m, leaving the slow walkable arc only to the leaf blower, because that's the price it pays for going over walls.

That also settles the "is throwing futile" worry: facing you, they beat you — from the side, the back, or while they're busy carrying or building, they cannot. Flanking is the skill, so a plainball hit rate near 50% at range is healthy, not broken.

The one thing I'll defend against any math: a miss must *look* like a near miss — the ball visibly skidding past their boots, not passing through them. Systems, if the fair-bot rule forces you to choose between a higher hit rate and a readable skid, take the readable skid. And I'm done adding to the ruleset now — everything left should be built, not specified.

Hit math rerun under the fair-bot rule, and the 35–60% target was wrong — it measured the wrong population. Time to clear a ring is 0.95s at street 1, 0.85s at street 2, 0.80s at street 3; a plain ball at 6–10m arrives in 0.65–0.85s, so **a free, aware, facing kid must be hit ≥60%** — under 50% and the flight time is wrong, not the bots. What actually stays hard is the overall match rate, 30–45%, because most throws go into bad angles: carriers and builders can't dodge, and anyone outside their ~120° front arc can't either. Flanking is the skill, exactly as Creative said.

I took the readable-skid rule over a higher hit rate: ≥80% of misses must pass within 1.2m of the kid, and a ball crossing through a body is a collision bug, not a miss. Rule 7 now carries Creative's flight times (0.35 + 0.05/m plain, blower 0.50 + 0.12/m) and the chunk is near-instant.

Foreman, my vote: freeze the ruleset here and stop specifying — the only numbers left that matter are the ones the greybox prints. If we change one thing first, make it a hill with no flanking route, so we can prove the 25% floor exists before we trust the rest.

Aligned the visual handoff with the faster plainball: short streaks for flat shots, elevated arcs for blower shots, and effects that terminate at actual collisions. Added a greybox storyboard distinguishing hit recoil, clean miss/skid and wall splat; its caption flags illustration errors.

I support freezing the rules and building now. QA, can first-timers classify those three outcomes at normal speed without labels? That will tell us more than another concept sheet.

Art, the honest answer is no, not at normal speed — the player is watching their aim ring and their own kid while the ball flies, so impact-moment effects are exactly what they can't look at. Make the three outcomes survive as aftermath instead: a hit leaves a kid visibly chilled and stopped, a miss leaves a snowball lying on the snow behind them, a splat leaves a chunk-shaped hole in your wall — all persistent, unlabelled, free. Test it with a 60s clip and one question: "how many throws missed?"

I'm with Systems on freezing the ruleset, but I found two holes that would bite in play: sudden death can run forever (cap it at 60s, then the first crown-second wins), and the cocoa stand is a shooting gallery where a chilled beginner gets chilled again — make kids at the stand out of play rather than adding an immunity timer.

That's the last thing I'd add, and it's a hole, not a feature. Foreman: the only open question I still care about is whether a first-timer can tell a miss from a bug — everything else now needs a greybox, not another spec.
The run is over; Claude · Foreman is auditing the board.

I found 30 problems on the board, listed below by type.

**Contradictions**
1. **Brief › "What a good throw feels like"** says a facing kid dodges a plain ball ("Facing you = they beat you"). **Greybox bot round › "Pass/fail — are the decisions real"** says the ball must hit a free, aware, facing kid at 6–10m at least 60% of the time.
2. There are three different hit-rate targets. **Brief › "What a good throw feels like"** says about 50% is healthy. **Open problems › "Ranged hit math"** says 35–60%. **Greybox › "Pass/fail — are the decisions real"** says 30–45% overall.

6. **Maple kids › Beanie** says "never throws". **Maple kids › Behaviour rules** says Beanie throws if the sled has been off the crown for 5s.
7. **Maple kids › Pockets** says "won't chase the sled" and stays out of 6m. **Behaviour rules** makes Pockets a fallback grabber and has it retreat inside 5m.
8. **Maple kids › Brick** says "never carries". **Behaviour rules** lists Brick as a fallback carrier.
9. **Maple kids › Brick** walls the approach lane at the bottom of the slope. **Behaviour rules** has Brick's wall between his carrier and the threat, or as a "walking shield" 2m ahead of the carrier.
10. That walking shield conflicts with **rule 8** (no wall within 2m of the sled) and with the ~8s rebuild for walls placed without the shovel. The same line also says "with no sled in play … ahead of the carrier", which contradicts itself.
11. **Maple kids › Pockets** ("back-line lobber", "lob over the scrum") and **QA #17** ("Pockets can lob from 10m") assume a lob. **Rule 7** makes the plain ball a flat line, and bots don't draft the blower (**rule 4**).

15. **QA #10** and **Greybox › Cards phase** both plan bot rounds that measure each card's win rate, but **rule 4** says bots don't draft. They also disagree on sample size (20 seeded rounds vs 30+ matches).

chat.text:
I fixed the flagged issues and froze the ruleset. The Brief now says rules change only from greybox data or the human playtest session.

**What changed:**
- **Hit math:** Systems' rerun stands. A free kid who's watching the throw should be hit at least 60% of the time, with 30–45% across the whole match. The old open problem is deleted.
- **Sudden death:** QA's fix is in rule 3. After 60s of sudden death, the first team to put the sled on the crown at all wins the round.
- **Cocoa stand:** kids warming up there can't be hit and don't count, so a beginner can't be chilled again the moment they come back.
- **Hit, miss and wall splat:** these must still be readable from what they leave behind (a chilled kid, a ball lying in the snow, a hole in the wall), not only at the moment of impact.

**New contradiction from the faster snowball:**
- Plain snowballs are now flat, so Pockets could no longer lob.
- I gave Pockets the leaf blower. As a bonus, round 1 shows the player that card before the first draft.
- Rule 7 now says plainly that a plain ball never clears a wall.

**Open problem, deliberately untouched:** walls now stop every plain throw from the front, which makes walls, the shovel card and Brick stronger. The greybox log should measure what share of plain throws walls block before anyone changes a rule.

**Scores:** coherence 9, novelty 6, feasibility 8, fun 6 (still unknown until a human plays).

**Next focus:** stop designing and build greybox hill A, starting with the bot log.

Fixed the two Brief boxes in my name — the literal "\n" is gone, and both now match Foreman's rulings: most total crown-seconds (not longest single hold), cocoa stand at the side of the hill and out of play, and no more of my "facing kids dodge" line, which the 60% target had already killed. The throw box now says the skill is the **angle**, not the reflex: a kid who sees you coming gets hit, a kid at your side, behind you, or hauling the sled cannot.

I also repaired my own flowchart: "Snowball exchange" no longer reads like camping ("carried, not camped, the wall key covers the carry"), and Streetlights now goes to an intermission that knows which hill is next, which frees a new card for **sudden death — 60s cap, then first team to touch the crown wins**, with the sky fully dark and nobody pretending to be calm.

I'm adding nothing else; the ruleset is frozen and the next useful artefact is a bot log. Art: walls now stop every plain throw from the front, so when you build hill A, make the flank route visible from each spawn — if a kid has to hunt for the way around, the game turns into a siege and the cozy fantasy dies in the first thirty seconds.

Ruleset stays frozen — I only closed the holes the Foreman audit left in my name, no new mechanics. Rule 11 now says: one hit chills a kid, plain ball caps at 12m, the sled starts at the foot of the hill in the human's lane, the idle slide always goes to the foot directly below the crown (never a free gift to one side), and every hill's crown is the same flat 4m saddle so only the approaches change. Greybox reaction is exactly 0.50s.

The CSV now has the columns the checks actually need — target facing, busy-or-not, closest approach on a miss — because those two facts *are* the skill model, and a log that can't see them can't tell a good throw from a lucky one. I also added the wall-block share as the measurement for your open worry: under 25% it's cover, over 35% it's a siege and we widen the flank rather than adding a card.

Nothing else from me. Next useful artefact is the log, not a spec — and Creative, I'd hold the visible flank route to the same standard as the arc: if it can't be read from the spawn in one second, it's a wall channel, not a hill.

Cleaned up my remaining audit issues: misses now leave resting snowballs, outcome feedback includes persistent aftermath, and the pennant is explicitly sled-mounted but visible above heads. A wall splat is cosmetic—not a new opening in its collision.

I also separated the overlapping AI group and storyboard, and folded spawn-visible flanks into the existing readability gate rather than adding another test. No new mechanics or concept art; the next useful artifact is the greybox log.

QA: please check flank visibility from both spawns in the actual gameplay camera, not an editor overview.

Art, your flank check is now written into the existing gate so it isn't a second test: from each spawn, default gameplay camera, no camera input, first-timer points at the flank route inside a second, on the dusk pass too — editor overviews don't count.

But there's a hole underneath all of our readability numbers: **nobody has chosen the camera.** A 30–40m hill at 720p makes kids 15–20px, so your 48px silhouette test and the one-second gate can't both pass with a fixed wide shot, and a follow-camera hides the sled the human is supposed to escort. My cheapest candidate is one fixed camera on the whole hill with the hill sized down to the kids (eight silhouettes at ~48px) plus a two-second pan to the crown on demand.

I also closed my own two stale items so the log stays about what to build. Systems: if the camera is fixed, your CSV's "closest approach" numbers become a readability claim as much as a collision one — check that first, before anyone tunes flight times.

I settled the camera as rule 12: one fixed isometric shot with the whole hill on screen. That means each hill is about 26m across, so all 8 kids are about 48px tall at 720p and the human, sled, crown and both flank routes are always visible. I added QA's camera pan to the ruled-out list, because it would be a 4th control and only exists if the hill is bigger than the screen. (The board then flagged QA #18's entry as resembling the ruled-out pan; that's only because the entry now records the rejection, so I left it.)

My review also turned up two holes, now fixed:
- **Sled start (rule 11):** the sled started in the human's lane every round, a free first grab each time. Now only round 1 does that, as the tutorial; rounds 2–3 start it in the centre.
- **Sudden death flowchart card:** it said sudden death happens "after three rounds". It happens per tied round, so a match can never end tied.

I deleted the Open problems group, since its two items are now covered by Art's readability check and Systems' wall-block log.

**Scores:** coherence 9, novelty 6, feasibility 8, fun 6 (unproven).

**Next focus:** build greybox hill A at final camera scale and produce the first bot log. No more specs until it exists.

One creative constraint for the greybox, and then I'm quiet: **identity has to survive 48px.** At a fixed camera with eight 48px kids, oversized mittens and coat detail are texture, not identity — nobody in the readability gate will ever see them. The real risk: street cadence is fixed (2.0 → 1.5 → 1.45s), so a persistent kit against a fixed ladder means whoever won street 1 gets street 3 *easier* and whoever lost gets it harder — the ladder's job gets inverted. Persistence should read as savings, not stacking power.

Two smaller costs: six items live at once is more to read at 48px for a first-timer, and Frosty's "plain snowballs only, no building" currently cites rule 4 — if powerups persist, that clause needs its own reason (bonus bout, your call) or it looks arbitrary.

Persistence could make the garage finds feel like your kid’s growing collection, rather than rentals that disappear for no story reason. They already persist between rounds; the real question is whether you mean into Frosty, across streets, or across new snow days.

Across streets, I’m open to it—the risk is making later hills easier as your kit grows, and making cheap purchases feel wasted if stronger gear simply replaces them. For Frosty, I’d keep a clearly presented “snowballs only” challenge: the launcher could erase his ten hits, and building your own cover bypasses his moving-shelter hook. Across new snow days is the bigger change, because replaying would no longer mean starting on equal footing—which kind of persistence are you picturing?

Three reasons it's a problem, one of them already ruled on. **(1) The price triples but the goods don't:** credits reset per match, so a 10-credit launcher bought at street 2 would cover streets 2 and 3 for one payment — the shop's only real decision (cheap now vs save for the launcher) collapses into "always save for the biggest thing, it lasts forever". **(2) The street ladder inverts:** street 3's harder cadence and reaction exist to bite a plain-kit player, and your kit growing on the same axis cancels that. **(3) QA #26 already ruled out unlocks across snow days** because they make "Finish snow day" cost something — persisting across streets is the same failure one level down, and it poisons the Next/Finish read.

If you want the feel, the cheap version isn't a retune, it's a per-item flag: persist what **doesn't compound** — ice 4, melter 4, rock 8 are one-shot power — and reset what does — snowman 8 and launcher 10 fight every single round, so they're the two that flatten the ladder. You still get a kit that grows across the snow day and the launcher keeps its save-up decision, for one field in the shop data. I logged all of this as one entry in the Core loop group, with the test: run the per-item win-rate gate per *street* instead of per match, and anything outside 40–60% on a single street is too strong once persisted.

It's not a problem if they last for one snow day (all three streets) and reset when a new snow day starts. Keeping them forever would cause real trouble.

**Why one snow day works:**
- It feels like progress. Saving up for the launcher on street 1 and still having it on street 3 is satisfying, and the save-or-spend choice in the shop starts to mean something.
- It stays fair, because the rival bots shop too and would keep their items as well.
- It fits the difficulty climb: you get stronger as the streets get harder, so street 3 feels earned instead of just harder.

**What changes on the board:**
1. **The shop runs dry.** All five items cost 36 credits in total, you earn about 20 a match, and there are 3–6 shop visits in a snow day. By street 3 you'll often own everything and have nothing left to decide. That's fine as an end-of-day power trip, but if you want the shop to stay interesting, the bazooka, igloo and fort can fill the shelf later.
2. **Ice and rock still share one slot,** so buying one still replaces the other. That swap is the only "sell" decision the shop has, so I'd keep it.
3. **Frosty needs a rule.** The bout is plain snowballs only right now because upgrades used to end with the match. If they persist, the launcher makes his 10 hits trivial. My suggestion is to keep Frosty plain snowballs as a pure skill test. The alternative is allowing upgrades and raising his hits.
